# Timing constants

*Generated by `python -m alien_remake --timing`. Do not edit by hand: `alien_remake.core.timing` is the source, and a test fails if this file falls behind it.*

The simulation runs at **7.886 Hz**, the rate measured off the real machine's main loop. Every duration below is counted against that.

The question this answers is T3's: **once a turn is however long the player takes, what does each of these numbers mean?**

## Loop counts — these survive player-paced turns

A counter the ROM decrements once per main-loop pass. The number means *N passes* and nothing else, so under turns it means *N turns* and every ratio between them is preserved. The Alien staying twice as fast as the cat is a property of these numbers, not of the clock.

| constant | value | now | what it times | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MOVE_ACTION_TICKS` | 64 | 8.1 s | a crew member walking to another room | [C $48F7] a flat $40 armed into the action counter, before the slot and health terms are added. **This is the natural unit of one turn's work** and the obvious thing to price AP against |
| `ATTACK_ACTION_TICKS` | 40 | 5.1 s | an ATTACK or a USE | [C $48F7 LDA #$28] the same counter, armed with $28 - so an attack is 40/64 of a move, a ratio that survives any re-pacing |
| `GRILLE_ACTION_TICKS` | 0, 100, 120, 180, 100, 180, 80, 80 | - | REMVGRILLE, per crew slot | a per-character table: the engineers are quick at it and the captain is slow. Characterisation expressed as duration, so it must survive as duration |
| `ACTION_DELAY_BY_SLOT` | 0, 7, 5, 0, 7, 3, 10, 5 | - | the per-crew-member surcharge on any action | [C $4032] added to every action's cost; who you send changes how long it takes, which is a mechanic and not flavour |
| `ACTION_DELAY_BY_HEALTH` | 0, 0, 48, 16, 0, 0, 0 | - | the wounded surcharge on any action | a hurt crew member is slower - 48 extra passes at 2 health, which nearly doubles a move |
| `ALIEN_MOVE_TICKS` | 60 | 7.6 s | the Alien's surface move timer | [C $8A4A] a counter reload. Its *ratio* to MOVE_ACTION_TICKS is the chase: the Alien moves about once for every crew move |
| `ALIEN_DUCT_TICKS` | 40 | 5.1 s | how long the Alien stays in a duct | a counter reload |
| `ALIEN_DUCT_TRAVEL_TICKS` | 70 | 8.9 s | duct-to-duct travel | a counter reload |
| `ALIEN_BURST_TICKS` | 40 | 5.1 s | the burst out of a grille | a counter reload |
| `ALIEN_PURSUIT_TICKS` | 20 | 2.5 s | how long it keeps chasing | a counter reload |
| `ALIEN_NET_ENTANGLE_TICKS` | 80 | 10.1 s | how long the net holds it | a counter reload |
| `ALIEN_ENCOUNTER_HOLD_TICKS` | 40 | 5.1 s | the pause on meeting the crew | a counter reload |
| `ALIEN_VENT_STUN_TICKS` | 120 | 15.2 s | how long a venting stuns it | a counter reload |
| `JONES_MOVE_TICKS` | 40 | 5.1 s | the cat changing rooms | a counter reload |
| `JONES_WALK_TICKS` | 5 | 0.6 s | the cat's walk animation step | presentation, not a rule |
| `PANIC_WANDER_TICKS` | 40 | 5.1 s | a panicking crew member wandering | a counter reload |
| `FIRE_SPREAD_EVERY_TICKS` | 256 | 32.5 s | how often an unfought fire eats another point | [C $5684] `INC $64CE / BNE rts` - it fires on the byte wrapping, so 256 passes exactly. A pure loop count, and the one that decides whether a fire is a crisis or a nuisance |
| `HEARTBEAT_DIVIDER_BY_COMPOSURE` | 4:40, 3:30, 2:23, 1:15, 0:15 | - | the heartbeat's IRQ divider, by composure | [C $4E16] paces voice 1's sound; a calmer crew member's heart audibly beats slower. Audio, not a rule |

## Calibrated to real seconds — these are what T3 must decide

The number encodes a wall-clock duration: a blocking `delay_long` (3.128 s on PAL hardware), a measurement against a real drive, or a figure the game says out loud. Detached from a fixed clock they mean nothing by themselves.

| constant | value | now | what it times | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AUTO_DESTRUCT_TICKS` | 2550 | 323.4 s | the whole self-destruct countdown | **the hard one.** Mechanically it is 10 wraps of a 255 counter, so it looks like a loop count - but the game *says* NINE MINUTES on screen, and a player who takes an hour over nine minutes' worth of turns has been told something untrue. Re-pacing turns makes this either trivial or unsurvivable, and it is a judgement, not a bug |
| `AUTO_DESTRUCT_SUBTICKS` | 255 | 32.3 s | one wrap of the countdown byte | [C $5A39] `LDA #$FF` - the reload the ten wraps are made of |
| `AUTO_DESTRUCT_MINUTES` | 9 | - | the number the game says out loud | the announced figure, which is what makes the countdown a promise about real time rather than about turns |
| `NOTICE_TICKS` | 12 | 1.5 s | how long a row-24 banner is held | [C $561C] one blocking `delay_long`; the remake cannot block, so it holds the banner for the equivalent instead. A reading time |
| `TITLE_TICKS` | 197 | 25.0 s | the whole title card | eight `delay_long`s = 25.0 s PAL. Front end, so T3 need not answer for it - but it is why the skip exists |
| `TITLE_LETTER_TICKS` | 25 | 3.2 s | the gap between title letters | one `delay_long` = 3.128 s PAL |
| `TITLE_REVEALED_TICKS` | 100 | 12.7 s | when the fifth letter has landed | four letter gaps; the point the skip fast-forwards to |
| `OPENING_TICKS` | 49 | 6.2 s | the opening death notice | [C $50B8/$50BB] two `delay_long`s = 6.256 s. A reading time |
| `INTRO_LEGEND_TICKS` | 197 | 25.0 s | the deck-plan key and sound legend | `delay_long`-paced, and a reading time |
| `LOADING_MENU_TICKS` | 111 | 14.1 s | the GREEN VALLEY spiral | [C-live] measured at ~14.1 s against the real disk - BASIC's POKE loop is genuinely that slow |
| `LOADING_PLAY_TICKS` | 20 | 2.5 s | the PLUG JOYSTICK card | [?] not paced by the ROM at all: it shows while the loader reads the next file, so its length is drive I/O. Left at a plausible 3 s |
| `EXIT_ADVERT_TICKS` | 25 | 3.2 s | the ONE-STEP DEALER advert | [C EXITO 1100] `FOR XX=1TO3000` before `SYS 64738` |
| `BOOT_TICKS` | 75 | 9.5 s | the remake's own startup card | not the original at all; a reading time chosen for this remake |
| `TURN_CREATURE_SLOT_TICKS` | 60 | 7.6 s | the Alien/Jones initiative slot's own tick ceiling | not the original at all - the disk has no turn-based mode, let alone initiative. Bounds how long a creature's autonomous slot runs before initiative passes on, chosen as a reading-time-scale window rather than derived from any ROM constant |
| `SCREEN_FX_GLITCH_TICKS` | 12 | 1.5 s | the `screen_fx` static flourish's own duration | not the original at all - a fixed, fading burst of static at the start of a screen entered with `screen_fx` on, chosen as a reading-time-scale flourish rather than derived from any ROM constant |
| `SCREEN_FX_CURSOR_BLINK_TICKS` | 4 | 0.5 s | the `screen_fx` typing cursor's blink rate | not the original at all - the conventional terminal-cursor blink rate, not derived from anything ROM-side |
| `SCREEN_FX_STRETCH_TICKS` | 5 | 0.6 s | the `screen_fx` CRT power-on stretch's own duration | not the original at all - how long the boot report takes to grow from a thin band to full height, a flourish scaled to stay well inside BOOT_TICKS's own timeout |
| `SCREEN_FX_SHAKE_TICKS` | 8 | 1.0 s | the `screen_fx` degauss shake's own duration | not the original at all - a decaying wobble riding along with the power-on stretch, in the same shape (miniaturised) as the CRT layer's own deck-change degauss transient |

## Rates — the clocks everything else is counted against

Under player-paced turns these stop being the pacing; the turn is.

| constant | value | now | what it times | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TICK_HZ` | 7.886 | - | the simulation's tick rate | the measured main-loop rate; every LOOP_COUNT below is counted against this and nothing else |
| `MAIN_LOOP_HZ` | 7.886 | - | the ROM's own main-loop rate | measured on real hardware; also the cursor's repeat rate, which is why the sound debounce is derived from it |
| `ANIM_HZ` | 6.666666666666667 | - | the sprite-animation rate | the 60 Hz jiffy divided by the ROM's 9-jiffy animation divider |
| `JIFFY_HZ` | 60.0 | - | the C64's IRQ rate | a fact about the machine, not about the game |
| `IRQ_JIFFIES_PER_ANIM_TICK` | 9 | - | jiffies per animation step | the divider between the two rates above |
| `SCREEN_FX_CHARS_PER_TICK` | 16 | - | the `screen_fx` typewriter's pace | not the original at all - the divider between the tick rate and how fast the boot/title/ending reveal types out, one character at a time |
